title: Can I make money flipping old houses in Malaysia?
excerpt: A 24-year-old bank employee wants to buy dated houses below market value, renovate them and resell within months. Sean explains why flipping only pays for contractors, and suggests selling property instead.

question.asker: From F, a viewer who wrote in on Instagram
question.context: F is 24, has worked at a bank for a year and a half, lives with his parents and has low expenses. He enjoys interior design and wants to buy abandoned or dated houses below market value, renovate them and sell at market price within about six months, rather than hold rentals for years. He hopes his job gives him better loan rates.
question.text: Is house flipping a viable way to make money in Malaysia, and can he take a long loan for a short flip?

answer.quote: Property investment was supposed to be slow.
answer.summary: For him, no. Flipping pays mainly for renovation contractors and interior designers who profit from the building work itself, while an outsider takes all the risk. Sean suggests he sell property as an agent instead: little risk, he learns the market, and his income depends on his own effort.

reasons.title: The numbers only work at the bank's valuation
reasons.body: If a house sells for RM800,000 but the bank values it at RM1 million, a buyer who qualifies for a RM900,000 loan has room for renovation. But a newcomer often doesn't know what a kitchen, roof, water tank or auto gate costs, and each one eats into the margin.

reasons.title: Tax on a quick sale removes much of the gain
reasons.body: Property gains tax is highest in the first years after the SPA, so on a RM100,000 gain perhaps RM30,000 goes in tax. The third and later loans also can't get 90% financing, which limits repeat flips.

reasons.title: The deals and the work are hard to find
reasons.body: Neighbours snap up genuinely cheap houses first. Contractors can abandon jobs, and coordinating cabinet makers, ceiling installers and electricians takes far more hours than people expect, while the instalment keeps running.

reasons.title: Contractors profit regardless
reasons.body: A builder or interior design firm prices the works at cost and knows from past projects what a house will fetch. An outside buyer pays their margin and still has to find a buyer after tax.

actions: Learn the difference between bank valuation and the price buyers actually pay nearby.
Check current property gains tax rates on sales in the first few years.
Consider working as a property agent part-time to learn the market with little risk.
If you still want to flip, partner with an experienced contractor rather than going alone.
caveat: A refurbished house in a good location can still sell above neighbouring prices, because buyers will pay to skip the hassle. Flipping isn't impossible, just poorly suited to a newcomer financing it alone.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #191. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as Sean stated them in November 2022; property gains tax rates and loan limits change, so check current ones. Sean refers to his work at The Makeover Guys, a furnishing company.
